title: Blindcap
concept: Every mushroom in this box has the same face. What differs is the shank buried under the loam, and the only way anyone learns a shank is to slide an iron pin in under the cap's brim and watch whether it sinks or stands proud. You plant six stools over six rounds — you alone saw the shanks in your own trough, everyone sees which player planted where — and you spend a stingy handful of turns either buying one bit of truth with a pin or committing a crown to a patch of ground you are only guessing about. A turn is one plant plus one of those two, never both, so every crown you place is placed on strictly less information than you could have had.
novelty: The oracle is the plastic itself: a probe pin dropped into an angled hole under a mushroom's brim either sinks to the hilt or stops proud, because the buried shank is or is not grooved at that band — a hidden-information reveal that no player adjudicates, cannot be misremembered, cannot be lied about, and stays on the board forever as public relief. Layered on top: a piece whose OWNER is public (a notch count bitten into the cap brim) while its TYPE is secret (grooves on the buried shank), so supply-counting deduction works with zero memory burden, and area-scoring crowns must be committed before the groves they claim are ever revealed. Searches run (queries from prior_art_search.sh, all through WebSearch): the mechanism verbatim ('players plant identical-looking mushroom pieces whose hidden underground shank profile is read by pushing angled iron pins into the board that either sink or stand proud'), the incidental rule as its own product pitch ('board game where you probe a hidden piece with a pin that sinks or stops to learn its identity mechanical deduction'), the other incidental rule as its own pitch ('board game where each piece's owner is public but its type is secret and players claim connected groups before the types are revealed'), the theme+mechanism combination ('mushroom fairy ring board game hidden species identity deduction plant identical caps abstract strategy'), and the plain titles ('Toadstone board game BGG' and '"Blindcap" board game'). Closest MECHANICAL comparable, and it is the real one: Black Box (Eric Solomon, Waddingtons mid-1970s / Parker Brothers, BGG 165) — a grid of hidden atoms probed by rays, learning by inference from probe results. But Black Box is one hider versus one seeker deducing a single fixed layout, the probe result is ANNOUNCED BY A PERSON (or a book, or a computer) rather than produced by the geometry, there is no placement, no ownership, no area scoring and no commitment-before-reveal — and crucially every player here is simultaneously a hider of their own six stools and a seeker against everyone else's. Stratego / L'Attaque are the classic public-owner-secret-type pieces, but a Stratego rank is revealed only by combat and only to the two combatants, and there is no board-scoring layer; Mastermind and its Animal Mastermind Towers descendants are single-code deduction with a human giving feedback pegs, no shared board and no placement. Theme is clean: Fairy Ring (Repos Production, 2024, BGG 419074) is card drafting and mushroom-village engine building with no hidden piece types; Undergrove (Elizabeth Hargrave, AEG, 2024) is tile placement and pick-up-and-deliver mycology; Morels (BGG 122298) is a card game. Title check turned up a genuine collision — 'Toadstone', a toadstool-and-toads card game on The Game Crafter — which is exactly why this is titled Blindcap; '"Blindcap" board game' returned no game of any kind (nearest hits BlindFold, Blind Business and Nyctophobia, none of which the compound reads as).

art_direction.form_language: Two materials in one plastic, told apart purely by curvature: everything that grew is swollen, radiused and fluted with no straight edge on it, and everything that was forged is faceted, tapered and hard. The loam tiles are thick slabs whose top face is broken into an irregular polygonal craquelure of 1.4mm-deep, 1.6-3mm-wide dried-mud channels, chamfered at every rim so a slab never reads as a printed plate. The stools are fat flat-topped domes with a heavy radiused brim, thick everywhere, no thin walls and no filigree. The pins are hex-shafted with a knurled disc head and a blunt taper. Nothing in the box is delicate.
art_direction.silhouette: A field of cracked earth studded with pale mushrooms of exactly one design, a few wearing small toothed crowns, and iron pins jutting out from under their brims at rakish angles like thorns driven into the ground — the amount of ironwork on the table is a picture of how much the players have found out.
art_direction.part_vocabulary: FIVE families, each separable by shape alone at arm's length. (1) loam_tile — the only flat, wide, cracked thing; a thick slab of dried mud, its sockets ringed by 2mm raised collars, reads as ground. (2) stool_* — the only domed things; a flat-topped cap on a hidden shank, brim floating a finger's height above the loam. All four species are DELIBERATELY identical above ground; they are told apart only after the harvest, by the annular grooves on the shank (none / upper / lower / both), which are 3mm-deep bands unmistakable at a glance once the stool is lying on its side. Player ownership is a separate axis, carried on the cap brim as 1, 2, 3 or 4 square bites 3mm wide and 2.5mm deep — countable from across the table and carrying no species information. (3) claim_crown — the only toothed ring; low, flat-topped, six 3mm points, sits on the cap's central boss, reads as a coronet against a dome and cannot be mistaken for a cap. Owner is 1-4 pierced Ø3 holes through its flat top. (4) probe_pin — the only faceted straight thing; hex shaft, blunt taper, knurled Ø-wide head, unmistakably a tool and not a piece. (5) spore_trough — the only object with a wall; a long boat with a high near lip carved in the same craquelure, cradling six stools on their sides shanks-inward and standing three crowns in slots, with the owner's notch count cut into the back wall.
art_direction.surface_treatment: Craquelure channels 1.4mm deep by 1.6-3mm wide across every loam_tile top face and up the outer back wall of every spore_trough, so ground and trough read as one material. Concentric growth rings 0.8mm proud on each cap top. Thirty-two radial gill ribs 1.0mm proud on the underside of the cap brim — visible in the shadow gap between brim and loam, which is where a player's eye goes when sliding a pin in. Owner bites 2.5mm deep in the brim edge. Shank grooves 3mm deep, generously chamfered so the pin tip is guided in rather than catching. Knurl 0.9mm on the pin head. No motif anywhere under 0.8mm.
art_direction.hero_shot: The board mid-game, shot low: a cracked field of identical pale caps, five or six iron pins splayed out from under brims at different heights — some driven flush, some standing proud — three caps wearing crowns, and in the foreground one stool lifted out and laid on its side beside its empty socket so the two grooves on its shank are readable. The photo has to say, without a word of rules, that the mushrooms are keeping a secret and the pins are how you get it out of them.

components.name: loam_tile
components.desc: A thick slab of cracked loam carrying a 3x3 grid of stool sockets, dovetailed on all four edges so any edge mates any edge (2 tiles make a 6x3 field, 3 make an L, 4 make a 6x6). Each socket is a plain blind bore that fully swallows a shank, ringed by a raised collar the stool's shoulder rests on. Two probe holes per socket are drilled from the TOP face down into the bore at 30-40 degrees from vertical — self-supporting, and never breaking through the underside, which stays solid and flat on the bed. The upper hole meets the bore at the shank's upper groove band, the lower hole at the lower band, and both hole mouths lie inside the radius of the planted cap's brim, so the brim roofs them and there is no sightline into a socket from any seat: a pin is slid in sideways through the shadow gap under the cap. CLEARANCE CONTRACT: a fully-proud pin's head radius, plus the head radius of the nearest neighbouring socket's pin, must be less than the socket pitch, and no pin at any insertion depth may enter a neighbouring cap's envelope.

components.name: stool_deadhead
components.desc: Flat-topped fluted cap on a plain ungrooved shank: both probe pins stand proud. Cap, brim, boss and shank diameter are identical to every other species; only the shank grooves differ, and they are buried whenever the stool is planted. Cap brim carries 1-4 owner bites; two per player, one per owner-mark variant pair.

components.name: stool_bracket
components.desc: Identical above ground; one annular groove at the UPPER band only, so the upper pin sinks and the lower pin stands proud. Two per player.

components.name: stool_inkcap
components.desc: Identical above ground; one annular groove at the LOWER band only, so the lower pin sinks and the upper pin stands proud. Scarce: exactly one per player, and a grove of them scores double.

components.name: stool_hollow
components.desc: Identical above ground; annular grooves at BOTH bands, so both pins sink. Scarce: exactly one per player, and a grove of them scores double.

components.name: claim_crown
components.desc: A low six-toothed ring that drops onto the boss on top of any planted cap and never moves again. Owner is 1-4 pierced holes through its flat top, matching that player's cap bites. Outer diameter stays well inside the socket pitch so a crowned cap does not foul a neighbour or a neighbour's pins.

components.name: probe_pin
components.desc: Hex-shafted iron pin with a knurled disc head and a blunt guided taper, long enough that when the shank blocks it, the head stands a clear thumb's width proud of the loam, and when a groove admits it, the head comes down almost to the brim's shadow. The two states must be unmistakable across a table. Sixteen is the whole shared supply for the game and it is not replenished.

components.name: spore_trough
components.desc: A boat-shaped personal tray with six side-by-side cradles holding stools lying down, shanks pointing toward the owner, and three upright slots for crowns. The near lip is taller than a stool lying in its cradle, so the owner reads their own grooves by looking down into the trough and no one seated opposite can see them. Owner notch count cut into the back wall.

setup.text: Join one loam_tile per player, edge to edge by their dovetails, on the middle of the table: two players make a 6x3 field of 18 sockets, three make an L of 27, four make a 6x6 field of 36. Every socket starts empty. Sockets are neighbours if their collars share an edge of the grid, and neighbouring across a tile join counts exactly the same as within a tile.

Each player takes one spore_trough and lays into its six cradles the identical supply every player gets: 2 stool_deadhead, 2 stool_bracket, 1 stool_inkcap, 1 stool_hollow, all shanks pointing toward the owner. Look down into your own trough and you can read every groove; from any other seat the near lip hides them. This composition is the same for everybody and is public knowledge for the whole game — what is secret is only which of your six you are planting each turn.

Each player takes the three claim_crowns whose pierced-hole count matches the bite count on their own stools' brims, and stands them in the crown slots of their spore_trough. No two players may take the same owner mark.
Put all 16 probe_pins in a heap in reach of everyone. This is the entire supply of probes for the game, shared by all players, first come first served, and it is never refilled.

Learn the shank code, which is the whole language of the game: the UPPER probe hole reads the upper groove band, the LOWER hole reads the lower band, and a pin sinks where there is a groove and stands proud where there is not. stool_deadhead has neither groove (proud, proud). stool_bracket has the upper only (sunk, proud). stool_inkcap has the lower only (proud, sunk). stool_hollow has both (sunk, sunk). So one pin never names a species: an upper pin splits the four into two and two, a lower pin splits them into the four common ones and the two scarce ones. The youngest player takes the first turn; play passes clockwise.

turn.text: PLANT — mandatory while you still have stools. Take one stool from your spore_trough, cupping your fingers over its shank as you carry it, and seat it in any empty socket on the field. Its shoulder rests on the collar and its brim floats above the loam. From this moment the shank is buried and nobody, including you, can see it again until the harvest — but the bites on its brim publicly and permanently record which player planted it.
Then take exactly ONE free action from the three below, or pass. You may never take two free actions, and you may never probe and crown in the same turn.

FREE ACTION — PROBE. Take one probe_pin from the shared heap and slide it in sideways through the shadow gap under any planted stool's brim, into that socket's upper or lower probe hole, whichever is still empty. Let go of it. If the shank is grooved at that band the pin sinks almost to the brim; if it is not, the pin stands proud. Everyone sees the result and the pin stays where it is for the rest of the game, so the board keeps the record for you. Any stool may be probed, yours or anyone else's, and each of a socket's two holes can be probed only once. If the heap is empty, nobody can probe again.

FREE ACTION — CROWN. Drop one of your claim_crowns onto the boss of any planted stool that does not already carry a crown — it may be a stool any player planted. A crown is never moved or removed once placed. You are claiming a patch of ground, not a mushroom.

FREE ACTION — PASS. Take nothing this turn. Note that a probe is public: the truth you buy with your own turn is handed to everyone at the table, which is why nobody wants to be the one who pays for it, and why crowns get placed on thinner information than anyone is comfortable with.

end.text: After six full rounds every player has planted all six of their stools and three sockets per player stand empty. Play one CLOSING ROUND in the same seating order: each player takes one free action only — probe, crown or pass — with no planting. The last seat therefore gets the final word of the game, which is the compensation for having had last pick of an empty field.

THE HARVEST. Lift every stool out of its socket and lay it on its side immediately beside its own empty socket, shank pointing outward, so its grooves are readable; any crown stays with its stool. Do not move a stool to another socket. Probe pins stay in the loam.

Work out the GROVES. A grove is a maximal set of stools of the same species whose sockets are connected through shared grid edges — orthogonally only, never diagonally, and across tile joins as freely as within a tile. A lone stool with no same-species neighbour is a grove of one. Every stool belongs to exactly one grove; groves that carry no crown are simply ignored.

win.text: Each grove that carries at least one claim_crown pays out, and a grove pays out once per owner no matter how many of that owner's crowns sit in it. Let n be the number of stools in that grove. If every crown in the grove belongs to ONE player, that player scores n x n for it — once, even if two of their own crowns sit in the same grove, which is a wasted crown. If the grove carries crowns of TWO OR MORE different players, the grove is contested and each of those players scores only n for it — once per player, so a player with two of their own crowns in the same contested grove still scores only n, not 2n; the second crown is likewise wasted. A grove of stool_inkcap or of stool_hollow — the two species every player owned exactly one of — pays DOUBLE whatever it would otherwise pay. Crowns never placed score nothing. Add up your groves; the highest total wins. Ties are broken first by the larger single uncontested grove, then in favour of the later seat in turn order.
